search_log: Searched "Stephen King The Stand third person omniscient narrator point of view scholarly" and opened relevant results.
Searched for authorized excerpts with "The Stand Stephen King excerpt publisher chapter one"; opened and inspected Penguin Random House's complete Chapter 1 excerpt.

Searched "The Stand third-person", "The Stand omniscient narrator", and "The Stand point of view third person"; opened BookRags and SuperSummary's explicit whole-book POV descriptions and the A.V. Club critical discussion.
Opened Stephen King's official work page to verify title, author, original publisher, and edition history; it was nondiagnostic for person.
Opened the Oxford Academic article "Translating Stephen King's The Stand to Quality TV"; it analyzed adaptation structure but did not directly establish the novel's grammatical narrative person.
Opened the USF thesis landing page "Standing Up With The King"; its downloadable text was inaccessible and the available abstract did not establish narrator person.

Targeted exact-phrase searches established that q00812 and q00841 are dialogue, q00820 is Joe/Leo's speech, q00846 is Dayna's direct thought, q00858 is quoted deathbed speech, and q00815 is Flagg's local interior thought.
Searches also found unauthorized full-text copies; they were used only to resolve local quotation boundaries and were not treated as classification evidence.
person_note: The controlling narration is nonparticipating third person, moving among many characters' perspectives. The Goodreads evidence includes clear external narration at q00834, q00843, q00851, and q00859, while its visible first-person passages resolve as dialogue or direct thought rather than an autonomous first-person narrative strand. The authorized publisher excerpt independently demonstrates sustained third-person narration, and multiple whole-book sources explicitly describe the same structure while treating diary material as local. The principal limitation is that the publisher excerpt is from the Complete and Uncut edition and covers only the opening, but the whole-book structural descriptions and supplied quotes provide interior and ending corroboration, with no evidence that the original abridged edition changed the controlling person.
